entries.d: Vanillylmandelic acid is a product of catecholamine metabolism that is excreted in the urine. Measuring it in a 24-hour urine collection helps diagnose and monitor treatment of catecholamine-secreting tumours, particularly phaeochromocytoma and neuroblastoma, as well as assess noradrenaline metabolism in certain clinical settings.
entries.p: Discard the first morning urine and note the time; collect every urination during the day/night, including the following morning's urine. The sterile container holds a pH<2 preservative, 6M HCl, and is kept cool until delivery. For a few days beforehand, avoid bananas, chocolate, citrus fruit, coffee and tea. Changes to medicines, including antihypertensives, are made only in consultation with the doctor. During collection, avoid intense physical exertion and stress.

entries.d: Examination of faeces in three preparations looks for starch granules, muscle fibres and fat droplets to assess the digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats. It helps investigate enzyme deficiency or intestinal/pancreatic disorders in chronic maldigestion, diarrhoea, fatty stools and weight loss.
entries.co: The stool sample is brought to the laboratory.
entries.p: Three days on a diet that includes all three food groups. Menu given in the source: breakfast 0.5 L milk, 1 egg, a bread roll with 3–5 g butter/margarine; at 10:00, 200 mL milk + 200 mL water + 40 g semolina; lunch 200 g minced veal with 15–20 g butter, 150–200 g mashed potatoes, bread/drinks as desired; afternoon as breakfast without the egg; dinner as breakfast with 1–2 eggs. Collect 3–5 g or 3–5 mL from three places in the stool into a sterile container, without overfilling; no contact with the toilet, water or urine.

entries.d: The test determines the composition of a urinary stone to help investigate how stones form and recur. The composition can give clues about metabolic disorders, infection or the involvement of medicines, and support the choice of treatment.
entries.sp: Whole urinary stone or stone fragments
entries.p: Hand in the whole stone. Rinse it with cold water and dry it for 24 hours at room temperature; keep it in a clean urine container, without liquid, gauze, paper, wrapping or adhesive tape. To collect it, urinate through dense sterile gauze, preferably folded; the first morning urine is important. Do not use gauze washed with detergent. Check carefully for small grains as well. Dry the filtered stone on the gauze for 24 hours; collection can be repeated over several days. Transport dried stones in a urine container kept at room temperature.

entries.d: The test measures mineral elements and metals in hair. The laboratory presents it as an indirect look at their accumulation over recent months and at environmental exposure, stressing that interpretation is affected by individual differences and external contamination of the hair.
entries.p: Wash the hair with an ordinary neutral shampoo, without zinc, selenium or medicinal ingredients. Do not use conditioner, masks, oils, sprays or anti-dandruff shampoo. The sample must be clean and completely dry. Dyed/chemically treated hair is not accepted; after treatment, wait for 8–12 weeks of regrowth.

entries.n: DUTCH Cycle Mapping (urinary hormones – full menstrual cycle)
entries.d: Tracks changes in oestrogen and progesterone across the menstrual cycle to assess the timing of ovulation and the luteal phase. It is used as additional information for irregular cycles, cyclical symptoms such as PMS and migraine, fertility difficulties or preparation for IVF.
entries.p: Self-collection with the kit and calendar according to cycle length/amenorrhoea: 21 urine samples after waking, and the last 4 at intervals on the fourth day of the new cycle, or on day 33 if there is no cycle. Apply the urine to filter paper and let it dry for 24 hours at room temperature. Discuss hormone therapy, glucocorticoids and supplements with your doctor; do not skip contraceptives without guidance. Before the last four samples, avoid creatine, bananas and legumes for 48 hours; on that day, limit fluids to 1.2 L and avoid alcohol/caffeine. Follow the kit's full instructions.

entries.n: DUTCH Cycle Mapping PLUS (salivary cortisol, urinary organic acids and hormones – full menstrual cycle)
entries.d: This profile tracks oestrogen and progesterone across the menstrual cycle, together with the daily cortisol rhythm and the cortisol awakening response. It is described for assessing cyclical symptoms, ovulation, fertility and the link between hormonal fluctuations and stress.
entries.sp: Dried urine on filter paper and saliva
entries.p: At home, 21 urine samples are collected after waking according to the calendar; the last four and 5–6 saliva samples on day 4 of the new cycle or on day 33 if there is no cycle. Dry the urine on paper for 24 hours at room temperature; freeze the saliva. Before the final day: no alcohol/intense exercise for one day; no creatine, bananas/legumes for 48 hours. On that day: no alcohol/caffeine, ≤1.2 L of fluids. Before saliva samples: no food/tooth brushing for 30 minutes; rinse 10 minutes before the pre-dinner/bedtime samples. entries.d: The profile combines urine and blood markers to assess metabolism and nutritional needs. It analyses organic acids, amino acids, fatty acids, oxidative stress, nutrient and toxic elements and neurotransmitter metabolites, providing additional information in fatigue, malabsorption and metabolic or nutritional disorders.
entries.p: Morning urine in the kit tubes and capillary blood on the same day. Keep to your usual diet; avoid strenuous exertion for 48–72 hours, extreme diets for 3–5 days, artificial sweeteners/MSG for 24–48 hours, foods rich in phenols/flavonoids (e.g. coffee, tea, chocolate, berries, onions, grapes, apples with the skin), bananas, pineapple, kiwi and nuts for 48 hours; seafood for 3–5 days, or longer if eaten regularly. Fast for at least 8 hours, optimally 10–12. Discuss medicines/supplements with your doctor, usually 2–5 days beforehand; antibiotics, antifungals, probiotics, digestive enzymes and acid blockers may interfere. Follow the kit's full instructions.

entries.d: NutrEval combines blood and urine biomarkers for a functional assessment of nutritional and metabolic status. The report looks at possible needs for vitamins, minerals, antioxidants and fatty acids, as well as markers of energy metabolism, digestion, oxidative stress and exposure to metals.
entries.sp: Venous blood (plasma, serum, erythrocytes or whole blood depending on the parameter) and first morning urine.
entries.p: Morning urine in the kit tubes, delivered within 1 hour; blood is taken at the laboratory. Fast for at least 8 hours, optimally 10–12. Practical recommendations are to avoid: extreme activity for 48–72 hours; extreme diets and seafood for 3–5 days; artificial sweeteners/MSG for 24–48 hours; foods rich in phenols/flavonoids, bananas, pineapple, kiwi, nuts/pecans for about 48 hours. When this is not possible, avoid large amounts for 24 hours beforehand. Discuss medicines/supplements with your doctor. Follow the kit instructions.

entries.d: Liquid-based cervical cytology to detect cell changes that may be precancerous or cancerous. It can also show inflammation or infection; results are reported using the Bethesda system with reference to the Papanicolaou classification, and suspicious findings may need further assessment.

Check availability in advance; for pregnant women, only a sample from the gynaecologist is accepted.

It is a screening test; abnormal findings may need follow-up, colposcopy or biopsy, and the result is interpreted by the doctor according to the patient's condition.
entries.sp: Cells from the surface and canal of the cervix/cervical swab.
entries.p: No vaginal pessaries for two nights beforehand; after finishing treatment, wait 72 hours before a check-up. No vaginal douching the evening before and no sexual intercourse for 24 hours. Preferably around day 10 of the cycle, at least 5 days after the end of menstruation; during menstruation only as advised by the doctor. On the morning of the test, wash the area with mild soap/warm water and put on clean underwear. Allow ≥6 weeks between two samples and report your last test. Check the collection point in advance; pregnant women bring a sample from their gynaecologist. Relax the pelvic muscles during sampling.

entries.n: EnviroTOX Burden profile – mycotoxins, toxic metals, organophosphate pesticides, phthalates, bisphenols and parabens in urine
entries.d: The presence of mycotoxins in urine does not prove mould-related illness or the source of exposure; this result is not sufficient for a diagnosis or for choosing a detoxification treatment.
entries.p: First urine in a sterile container, ≥6 hours after the last urination, before food/drink. Reduce fluids after 18:00 and empty the bladder before sleep. Postpone if the urine contains blood. Do not stop medicines without consulting your doctor; after cefalexin, wait ≥4 days. Avoid supplements and toxin binders for ≥3 days, unless instructed otherwise. Avoid fish/seafood for ≥1 week; after gadolinium contrast, wait ≥96 hours. Fasting for about 12 hours is optional. Before collection, avoid cosmetics on the hands, strong chemicals/detergents and contact with plastic. Close, label and deliver the container.

entries.d: TOXDetect measures 27 metabolites of organophosphate pesticides, phthalates, bisphenols and parabens in urine to assess recent exposure. It does not identify the exact source, and the presence of metabolites does not necessarily mean disease; interpretation requires exposure history and clinical information.
entries.p: First morning urine in a sterile container, ≥6 hours after the last urination, before food/drink. Reduce fluids after 18:00 and empty the bladder before sleep; close, label and deliver the sample. If blood is visible, postpone the test. No special fasting or routine discontinuation is needed; do not change medicines without consulting your doctor. After cefalexin, wait ≥4 days from the last dose. Immediately beforehand, where possible, avoid cosmetics/lotions on the hands, strong chemicals/detergents and contact with plastic packaging that may contain phthalates/bisphenols.

entries.d: Renin is part of the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system, which regulates blood pressure and the balance of water and electrolytes. entries.p: Blood is taken in the morning on an empty stomach. At least 30 minutes lying down before the sample, rest and avoiding stress are recommended. Inform the doctor about your diet and any use of ACE inhibitors, diuretics, beta blockers or other medicines that may affect renin.

entries.d: Examines prostate secretion for bacteria and fungi when there are urinary symptoms, recurrent infections or perineal and pelvic pain. When clinically significant bacteria are found, antibiotic sensitivity testing is carried out to support the choice of treatment.
entries.p: Taken by the urologist after hygiene and prostatic massage, on a swab/in a sterile container, with urine before/after according to the 2- or 4-glass test. The 4-glass test includes 5–8 mL of initial stream, midstream, secretion and 2–3 mL after massage; the 2-glass test describes midstream, secretion and 2–3 mL after massage. Transport within ≤2 hours at room temperature. No urination for ≥2 hours, no ejaculation for 2 days, no genital creams for 1 day. Contraindicated in acute prostatitis; midstream first morning urine is recommended.

entries.n: Throat swab – group A streptococcal antigen, rapid test
entries.d: This rapid test looks for group A streptococcal antigen in a throat swab, helping to tell whether a sore throat has a streptococcal cause. It is an indicative test: it can be positive in carriers without symptoms and negative when the amount of bacteria is low.
entries.p: Swab from the back wall of the pharynx/tonsils, in the morning before eating and brushing teeth; during the day, at least 2 hours after food/drink. Beforehand, do not use oral antibacterial preparations, drops, sprays or antiseptic mouthwashes. During sampling, keep the mouth open and the tongue down; a child sits on the parent's lap with the head and hands supported.

entries.d: A nasal swab culture looks for pathogenic bacteria on the lining of the nose when a bacterial infection of the nose or sinuses is suspected. It may be used for thick discharge, small sores or a burning feeling in the nose; an antibiogram (antibiotic sensitivity test) is performed on any bacteria isolated.
entries.p: Staff use a sterile swab without touching the nasal entrance during insertion. The child is held on the lap with the head and arms steadied by the parent, as directed by staff.

entries.d: Looks for fungi of the genus Candida in secretions from the lining of the nose, using a nasal swab culture. The report states whether Candida was isolated and, if present, describes the amount as small, moderate or large.
entries.p: Sterile swab in both nasal cavities, about 1–2 cm deep, rotated for 10–15 seconds. Transport within 2 hours; if delayed, in transport medium at room temperature for up to 24 hours. No other preparation; ≥12 hours after a local antiseptic or rinsing with saline solution.

entries.p: Serum from venous blood. During thyroid therapy, follow the doctor's schedule, usually before the next dose. During an acute illness, the need for and timing of the test are decided by the doctor, especially if a thyroid cause is suspected.

entries.n: Adrenal stress test – salivary cortisol, 2 samples
entries.d: This two-sample test measures free cortisol in saliva in the morning and evening, to compare the daily rhythm of secretion. The laboratory offers it as part of a functional assessment of fatigue, sleep and the stress response; results are interpreted according to the history and clinical picture.
entries.p: Home kit: 07:00–09:00 and 23:30–00:30, about 2 mL in each tube. Reduce foam by tapping gently; close/freeze the samples immediately and keep them frozen until delivery. For 30 minutes beforehand: no food/drinks other than water, smoking, chewing gum, sweets, tooth brushing, mouthwash or lip cosmetics. Rinse the mouth with cold water 10 minutes before. The saliva should be clear, without mucus; avoid coughing, intense exertion and stress. Insufficient samples are not analysed.

entries.d: Tracks oestradiol and progesterone in 11 saliva samples over the cycle, as well as testosterone at the start of the cycle. It aims to provide information on ovulation, the luteal phase and hormonal balance in irregular cycles, difficulty conceiving or premenstrual symptoms.
entries.p: Home kit with 11 samples on set days, usually starting on day 3; label and freeze immediately. Deliver frozen as soon as possible, ideally the morning after the last sample; accepted every day. For 30 minutes before: no food, drinks other than water, tooth brushing or chewing gum. entries.n: Zonulin peptides (Zonulin Family Peptide – GI Effects add-on test)
entries.d: Zonulin Family Peptide is an add-on stool test, offered only together with GI Effects, for zonulin-like peptides. The laboratory presents it as a functional assessment of the intestinal barrier in chronic digestive complaints and for monitoring changes during clinical interventions.
entries.sp: Faeces, usually from the same GI Effects sample.
entries.p: Use the GI Effects kit and follow the instructions for collecting, storing and delivering the faeces without contamination by urine or water. Do not interrupt any therapy on your own.
